title: Towards Reliable LLM Evaluation: Correcting the Winner’s Curse in Adaptive Benchmarking
topic: Data-centric AI->Data-centric AI methods and tools
claim: A multi-stage protocol tunes, freezes a shortlist, scores with repeated splits, then bootstraps items to give valid inference.
layout: 7 lettered panels in three stacked bands, left-to-right flow, downward arrows
description: The figure has three horizontal bands, each tinted differently. The top band, in gray with orange sub-boxes, is the tuning and evaluation phase. Panel (a) is the search phase: budget B, a tuning sample D, a tuner, prompts, an LLM and scores, with a feedback loop of artifacts. Panel (b) freezes the shortlist as Artifact 1 to K, with a calculator icon. Panel (c) is a matrix of per-item scores S for each artifact over evaluation items W1 to WM. A blue middle band, panel (d), is a left-to-right chain of boxes for repeated-split scoring and selection, with the selection and held-out formulas. A green bottom band covers inference. Panel (e) is the aggregated split-wise estimator. Panel (f) is the Gaussian multiplier bootstrap with item-level contributors and multipliers. Panel (g) lists the outputs: pointwise CI, simultaneous band and fixed comparisons. Bold arrows connect the panels, and the eye starts at the top-left.
caption: Overview of SIREN. Panels (a)-(b) show tuning with budget B and freezing the shortlist for one system j; panel (c) shows the per-item scores of its retained artifacts on evaluation items W1, . . . , WM; panels (d)-(e) show scoring, held-out evaluation, and aggregation for splits r = 1, . . . , R; panels (f)-(g) stack the item-level contributions across all N systems and budgets for bootstrap inference.
abstract: Adaptive prompt and program search makes LLM evaluation selection-sensitive. Once benchmark items are reused inside tuning, the observed winner's score need not estimate the fresh-data performance of the full tune-then-deploy procedure. We study inference for this procedure-level target under explicit tuning budgets. We propose SIREN, a selection-aware repeated-split reporting protocol that freezes the post-search shortlist, separates splitwise selection from held-out evaluation, and uses an item-level Gaussian multiplier bootstrap for uncertainty quantification. In a fixed-shortlist regime with smooth stabilized selection, the estimator admits a first-order item-level representation, and the bootstrap yields valid simultaneous inference on a finite budget grid. This supports confidence intervals for procedure-performance curves and pre-specified equal-budget and cross-budget comparisons. Controlled simulations and MMLU-Pro tuning experiments show that winner-based reporting can be optimistic and can change deployment conclusions, while SIREN remains close to the finite-sample reporting target.
